description: Somos un grupo de amigos estudiantes, que buscan mejorar el desarrollo de sus habilidades constantemente, nos gustan los desafíos y los retos. No somos expertos en la materia, pero somos buenos en aprender, proponer ideas y llevarlas a cabo. Nos gusta el trabajo en equipo, la resolución de problemas y sobre todo la sana convivencia. Un abrazo y éxito para los otros equipos.
summary:
We developed AstroHealth, a monitoring software prototype designed to support astronaut health during space missions. It integrates wristband, helmet visor, and spacecraft console interfaces to display health and well-being indicators, including vital signs, radiation exposure, sleep, and physical activity.

We addressed the challenge through an interactive simulation that demonstrates how the system identifies changes in these indicators, generates alerts, and helps crew members coordinate their response to emergencies. It also includes historical records and daily routines with shared goals that encourage healthy habits and teamwork.

Our project matters because it brings clear, accessible information together in an environment where every crew member’s well-being is essential to mission success. AstroHealth aims to strengthen crew autonomy and support an organized response to potential risks, combining individual care with collective support
details:
AstroHealth is a software prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring and teamwork during space missions. It combines a spacecraft console, a wristband interface, and a helmet visor interface to make health information accessible during different mission activities.

The system monitors eight indicators: heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, blood pressure, glucose, sleep, physical activity, and accumulated radiation exposure. The console gives an overview of five crew members, reflects what the wristband and helmet interfaces report, and shows individual alerts. Users can also switch between simulated camera views of the five crew members to see their perspectives.

When a critical condition or signal loss occurs, AstroHealth alerts the crew. Astronauts can acknowledge the notification, view the affected person's information, and indicate they are on their way to help. The system logs these responses and tracks the incident, supporting an organized team response. The helmet interface also shows simulated spacewalk oxygen levels and reserve warnings.

Beyond emergency monitoring, AstroHealth encourages daily exercise, sleep, hydration, and mood check-ins through routines, points, badges, and shared goals. Rewards recognize participation and supportive actions rather than a person's health status.

We developed AstroHealth in Python, using Tkinter for the desktop interfaces, SQLite for data storage, and OpenCV and Pillow for video playback in the helmet visor. A local web interface lets a phone act as the wristband during our in-person demonstration. The interactive simulation allows us to demonstrate normal conditions, health alerts, and signal loss.

The project's creativity lies in combining health monitoring, simulated crew perspectives, coordinated assistance, and daily wellness routines in a single experience. Our design prioritizes readability, large controls, clear alert levels, notifications when the signal is lost or no data is available, and access to essential information without overwhelming the astronaut.

AstroHealth's expected impact is to strengthen crew autonomy, encourage mutual support, and help astronauts recognize and respond to potential risks. By connecting individual care with teamwork, the project explores how accessible software can support safer space missions.
